about: Single source for the Washington Fishing Year artifact. Dated seasons and rules are artifact-only and are never read by the app (the app shows month ratings, not authoritative dates). A stop with site_id takes its coordinates from site/data/sites.json; a stop with site_id null keeps its own lat/lon because WDFW's access layer does not list it. Build: scripts/build_fishing_year.py.

seasons.name: Skagit coho
seasons.note: WDFW’s current order, effective Oct 18, allows 2 salmon a day from the mouth to the Marblemount Bridge, coho only, with no bait and single barbless hooks. It runs through Oct 31 unless WDFW extends it. In 2025 it ran to Nov 30 and closed Nov 19 when the catch guideline was reached, so go early. The Gilligan Creek to Baker River stretch is closed Oct 19 to 21 for a tribal fishery.

seasons.name: Chum
seasons.where: Hood Canal south of Ayock Point; south Sound rivers not checked
seasons.note: Mildest flavor, best smoked or cured. In the 2026 pamphlet chum can be kept in Hood Canal south of Ayock Point from Oct 16 to Nov 30, four salmon a day with Chinook released (coho too in November). Marine Area 13 requires chum to be released. Quality drops as the fish darken.

seasons.name: Winter steelhead
seasons.where: Olympic Peninsula rivers, some Puget Sound rivers
seasons.note: Most major areas were open Dec 1 to Mar 31 in 2025-26, but the Humptulips closed Feb 2 and the Chehalis Feb 16. Release wild fish and keep up to two hatchery steelhead a day.

seasons.name: Yellow perch
seasons.note: Open year-round. WDFW says fishing is best in summer after the perch spawn in April and May, and the catch drops in the fall. Very good fried.

seasons.name: Spring Chinook
seasons.where: Columbia, Cowlitz and Lewis rivers, 2.5 to 3 hours south
seasons.note: The best-tasting salmon. In 2026 the Columbia ran Mar 1 to Apr 8 below Beacon Rock and Apr 1 to 26 plus May 2 above it. WDFW expected spring Chinook fishing on the Cowlitz, Kalama and Lewis rivers but gave no dates. The 2027 dates are an estimate, so check the Columbia River rules.

seasons.name: Lingcod
seasons.note: Firm white flesh and the best non-salmon eating on this list. Off Westport (Marine Area 2) the 2026 season ran Mar 14 to Oct 17 with two a day, and WDFW sets it as the second Saturday in March to the third Saturday in October. Puget Sound has a shorter window.

seasons.name: Black rockfish
seasons.note: Pair it with the lingcod trip. Off Westport the 2026 season ran Mar 14 to Oct 17 with a daily limit of seven, and no more than five canary and no yelloweye. Copper, quillback and vermilion rockfish cannot be kept in May, June and July.

seasons.name: Walleye
seasons.note: WDFW says walleye fishing peaks before and after the April spawn, is excellent in summer with a lull in the heat, and improves in fall. One of the best-tasting freshwater fish. Plan a weekend trip.

seasons.name: Stocked trout
seasons.note: Easy from shore. Lowland lakes opened April 25 in 2026, and the 2027 date is estimated as the fourth Saturday in April. Check WDFW stocking reports for which lakes got fish.

seasons.name: Kokanee
seasons.where: Lake Whatcom, Lake Chelan, Lake Roosevelt
seasons.note: Landlocked sockeye with a sweet flavor, mostly trolled. WDFW says the kokanee fishery typically runs April to October, and Lake Chelan is usually best from mid-April through June. Not checked: restrictions on Lake Sammamish and Lake Washington.

seasons.name: Dungeness crab
seasons.where: Everett, Edmonds and the San Juans
seasons.note: In 2026 the Deception Pass, Everett and Admiralty Inlet areas ran July 2 to Sept 7, Thursday to Monday. The south San Juans ran July 16 to Sept 28, Thursday to Monday. Seattle was Sunday and Monday only, July 5 to Sept 7, and Tacoma ended Aug 17. You need a license, a Puget Sound Crab Endorsement and a catch record card. Limit is five males, 6¼ inches.

seasons.name: Baker Lake sockeye
seasons.note: In 2026 Baker Lake opened July 11 and ran to Aug 31, four sockeye a day, and opened whatever the fish count. The 2027 dates are an estimate, so verify them and the daily limit.

seasons.name: Pink salmon
seasons.where: Edmonds and Mukilteo beaches, Green and Nisqually rivers
seasons.note: Odd years only. Mild flavor, so eat it fresh.
seasons.pending: WDFW sets the 2027 odd-year pink seasons in April 2027, so there is nothing to check yet. The dates here are an estimate from the 2025 season.

seasons.name: Fall Chinook
seasons.where: Lewis River; Cowlitz and Olympic Peninsula rivers see note
seasons.note: In the 2026 pamphlet the Lewis River allowed hatchery Chinook from Aug 1, and from Oct 1 to Dec 31 one Chinook a day within an adult limit of three. The Cowlitz required release of all salmon except hatchery coho from Aug 1 to Dec 31. Olympic Peninsula rivers were not checked. Most Seattle-area rivers restrict Chinook, so plan to drive south or west.

seasons.name: Fall coho
seasons.where: Skagit River; other Puget Sound rivers not checked
seasons.note: In the 2026 pamphlet the Skagit coho season ran Aug 16 below Gilligan Creek and Sep 16 above it, to Oct 31, with a limit of 4 and then 2 in October. WDFW extended it to Nov 30 in 2025, and can close it on short notice. Check emergency rules before each trip.

milestones.label: Check Skykomish and Snoqualmie
milestones.note: WDFW closed both for summer and fall 2026 to protect wild Chinook. The Skykomish coho opener was moved to Nov 1 and is not confirmed. WDFW also closed the Snohomish River below them to all fishing from Oct 3 to Nov 1 over coho concerns. See whether any of them reopens.

milestones.label: Renew fishing license
milestones.note: The new license year starts Apr 1. Add the Puget Sound Crab Endorsement if you plan to crab.

rivers.name: Green
rivers.blurb: From Elliott Bay up through Kent and Auburn. The rules change by reach, so read the table below before you pick a spot.

rules.reach: Harbor Island line to Tukwila Int’l Blvd
rules.take: Daily limit 6, up to 3 adult coho and chum combined. Chinook released.

rules.reach: Tukwila Int’l Blvd to S 212th St bridge
rules.take: Daily limit 6, up to 3 adult coho and chum combined. Chinook released.

rules.reach: S 212th St to Hwy 18 eastbound bridge
rules.take: Up to 3 adult coho and chum combined. Chinook released.

rules.reach: Hwy 18 bridge to Auburn–Black Diamond Rd
Auburn–Black Diamond Rd to Tacoma boundary marker
rules.take: Game fish closed Sep 16 to Oct 31. Then coho and chum. Closed within 150 ft of the Keta Creek mouth.

rivers.rulesNote: Night closure and an anti-snagging rule applied on the Green last year. Best timing: coho peak now through early November, chum peak mid to late November, and both fade in December. Fish dawn and dusk, on weekdays, and the day after a rain. That timing comes from angler reports, not a WDFW forecast.

stops.name: Three Friends Fishing Hole
stops.note: Kent bank access by the S 212th St rule line; check the reach. Fish weekday dawns and the day after rain.

stops.name: Green River Boat Ramp
stops.note: A concrete hand-launch ramp, good for a small raft or kayak.

place_check.note: Searched for a Green River boat ramp in Kent and found no page naming one; the OpenStreetMap lookup failed on 2026-10-18 and was not retried.

stops.name: Isaac Evans Park
stops.note: City park on the river. One reviewer saw pinks caught here. On the map it is downstream of Hwy 18, but confirm the reach in the WDFW table.

rivers.line_mouth_note: the tidal Duwamish from Elliott Bay to Tukwila; rivers.json's Green River starts at Tukwila

rivers.name: Snoqualmie
rivers.blurb: Runs north from the Falls through Fall City and Carnation to join the Skykomish. Closed to salmon fishing below the Falls this fall, so the stops below are for scouting or the other seasons.

rules.take: WDFW closed it for summer and fall 2026 to protect wild Chinook and coho, along with the Tolt and Raging rivers. It reopens only if WDFW says so in season.

rivers.rulesNote: Gamefish was moved to Dec 1 this year, from Nov 1 last year. The Snohomish River from its mouth to where the Skykomish and Snoqualmie meet is closed to all fishing from Oct 3 to Nov 1.

stops.name: McCormick Park
stops.note: River park in Duvall, the lowest stop on this stretch.

place_check.name: McCormick Park
place_check.note: Coordinates moved 616 m to the park in Duvall; the old point was 147 m from the river, this one is 7 m

stops.name: Chinook Bend Natural Area
stops.note: Natural area on the river north of Carnation.

stops.name: Snoqualmie River Boat Launch
stops.note: Boat launch with free parking, close to where the Tolt joins.

place_check.name: unnamed slipway, with the Tolt River boat launch trail 107 m away
place_check.note: The Mountaineers and a paddling guide also place a free launch at the Tolt confluence in Carnation, river mile 25.

stops.name: Richter, WDFW access
stops.note: WDFW site with a concrete ramp. Check the signs for parking pass rules.

stops.name: Zurfleuh Boat Launch (WDFW “Raging River”)
stops.note: WDFW lists this as “Raging River”. It sits at the Raging River mouth.

stops.name: Plum #1 River Access Point
stops.note: Needs a Discover Pass.

rivers.name: Skykomish
rivers.blurb: East from Monroe to Gold Bar. Closed this fall to protect wild Chinook. The coho opener was pushed back to Nov 1 and is not confirmed.

rules.reach: Mouth to Wallace River, and Wallace River to the N/S Fork confluence
rules.take: WDFW closed the mainstem for summer and fall 2026. The coho opener moved to Nov 1, and I could not confirm it will happen.
Up to 2 coho, Chinook and chum released. WDFW’s June notice also lists the Wallace as closed, so confirm before you go.

rivers.rulesNote: The planned Reiter Ponds hatchery steelhead fishery is also closed this year. The Snohomish River from its mouth to where the Skykomish and Snoqualmie meet is closed to all fishing from Oct 3 to Nov 1.

stops.name: Lewis Street boat ramp
stops.note: Public boat ramp. It is busy on Saturday mornings in fishing season.

stops.name: Al Borlin Park
stops.note: Park with river access just upstream of the Lewis Street ramp.

stops.name: Ben Howard Hole, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW site with a concrete ramp.

stops.name: Jonker, WDFW access
stops.note: WDFW bank access at Sultan.

stops.name: Big Eddy
stops.note: Discover Pass, or $10 for parking.

rivers.name: Puyallup
rivers.blurb: From Commencement Bay up the valley. The salmon season ends Oct 31, so this is the last two weeks.

rules.reach: 11th St Bridge to East Main St Bridge, and East Main St Bridge to Carbon River
rules.take: Closed Tuesdays through Sep 30. Wild Chinook and chum released. WDFW cut the adult salmon limit to 2 this year because there are no pinks in an even year.

rules.reach: Carbon River, mouth to Voight Creek
rules.take: Closed Tuesdays through Sep 30. Same release rules.

rivers.rulesNote: Night closure and an anti-snagging rule applied last year.

stops.name: Two Rivers Point
stops.note: Beach-style access on the river.

place_check.note: Sumner's 2024 parks plan and TrailLink name Two-Rivers Point as the south end of the Sumner Link Trail; its coordinates were not checked.

stops.name: Sumner Sportsmen’s, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access site.

stops.name: Weiss, WDFW
stops.note: An unimproved WDFW access, so expect a rough bank.

stops.name: Foothills Trail, McMillin Bridge trailhead
stops.note: Not a WDFW site. A levee walk from the trailhead leads down to the river and its sand bars. A reviewer who fished the opening saw about one other person.

rivers.name: Skagit
rivers.blurb: The Skagit from the bay up into the Cascades. Lower river catches fish first, and the upper river is closest to spawning water.

rules.take: Daily limit 2 salmon, and you may keep coho only. Release all other salmon. No bait, and single-point barbless hooks only.
Closed to all fishing Oct 19 to 21 to avoid gear conflicts with tribal fisheries. Otherwise the same rules: 2 salmon, coho only, no bait, barbless single-point hooks.
Daily limit 2 salmon, coho only. No bait, and single-point barbless hooks only.

rivers.rulesNote: These come from WDFW emergency rule WSR 26-21-045. The Cascade River allows 4 coho a day and is open seven days a week. In 2025 WDFW extended the Skagit season to Nov 30, then closed all salmon on Nov 19 when the catch guideline was reached, so it can close early again.

stops.name: Spud House launch, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW concrete launch on the lower river, below Young’s Bar.

stops.name: Young's Bar River Access
stops.note: Wade out and cast. One reviewer caught salmon here on gold and orange spoons.

stops.name: Skagit River Park, Burlington
stops.note: Near the tideline, just upstream of the I-5 bridge. Fresh fish arrive here first.

stops.name: Sedro-Woolley access, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access with a concrete ramp.

stops.name: Gilligan Creek access, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access at a rules boundary. The season reaches change at Gilligan Creek, so check both sides.

stops.name: Lyman Ferry, WDFW access
stops.note: Slow water, and you can drive to the water’s edge for bank fishing.

stops.name: Hamilton Boat Launch
stops.note: Boat ramp and river access. Reviews of the area are mixed, so look it over in daylight first.

stops.name: Skagit–Baker confluence, Concrete
stops.note: Easy low-bank access at the mouth of the Baker River.

stops.name: Public fishing access, Concrete (WA-20)
stops.note: Bank access that reviewers say produces steelhead and salmon. Go on a weekday to avoid crowds.

stops.name: Howard Miller Steelhead Park, Rockport
stops.note: County park on the river with a boat ramp and campground.

stops.name: Marblemount boat launch
stops.note: The upper end, close to spawning water. Check for closed zones before you go.

rivers.line_mouth_note: the delta to Skagit Bay; rivers.json's Skagit River ends where the forks split and the page draws one simplified path
